A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAVRL and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial reformatting and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-learning experiments across six environments, including policy returns, EPIC distances, dynamics-perturbation tests, reward visualizations, and appendix feedback-budget sweeps.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across the same environments, including revised performance results and new baseline comparisons, equal-budget evaluations, and feedback-misspecification tests.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated encoder input from (s,a,s') to (s,a), including its use in the TD likelihood. This is a limited specification correction: v1 Appendix A.1 already described state-only or state-action rewards. Algorithm 1, the shared variational objective, and the principal method components remain unchanged; an implemented redesign is not established.

E1.justification: The same six environments and four feedback modalities remain. v2 adds evaluation under corrupted preferences, demonstrations, ratings, and stop signals, individually and jointly, on the three grid environments. These extend the feedback conditions tested without introducing new domains or tasks. Grid-trap dynamics perturbations already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 introduces substantive comparisons absent from v1: MCMC on all three grid environments and Post-Hoc Reward Averaging on those grids plus LunarLander-v3. The existing feedback-subset comparisons and behavioral-cloning baseline in transfer experiments remain.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces fixed network widths and a two-value regularizer search with joint Optuna searches over widths, regularization, optimizer settings, and policy-training parameters. LunarLander preference and rating budgets change from 1024 to 256 each. Appendix A.2 changes rating generation from deterministic quantile assignment to stochastic cumulative-logit sampling. New equal-budget and corruption experiments introduce additional allocation and testing protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds an equal-total-budget ablation testing whether complementarity merely reflects more supervision, and individual/joint feedback-corruption tests examining compensation and failure modes. Dynamics-robustness curves are revised. Conversely, v1 Appendix E's extensive feedback-budget sweeps disappear. The qualitative reward-map analyses are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix C newly specifies 20 tabular and 10 non-tabular seeds per tuning trial. Main results and transfer figures retain n=10, and standard-error reporting continues. Table 4 also states n=10, leaving its relationship to the 20-seed tuning description unclear; the PDFs do not establish an increase in final evaluation replication.

E6.justification: Main returns, EPIC distances, and transfer curves change extensively. For example, full-feedback grid_cliff return changes from 90.8 to 100.0 and CartPole from 87.5 to 100.0, while grid_trap EPIC changes from 0.432 to 0.520. These are revised results under changed protocols, not isolated same-setting gains. Baseline, equal-budget, and corruption results are added, while the earlier budget-sweep entries are removed.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects the ordered-logit definition from finite outer cutpoints to psi_0 = -infinity and psi_K = +infinity, ensuring the categories cover the full utility range. This is a mathematical correction beyond equivalent notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: unified Bayesian learning from heterogeneous feedback, scalable amortized inference, complementary reward information, improved downstream behavior, and interpretable uncertainty. Additional experiments do not redefine these stated core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now explains the noise-model and regularization parameters remaining despite avoiding cross-modal loss weights. Sections 6.2–6.3 add interpretations of ensemble failure, environment-dependent benefits under equal budgets, and compensation for corrupted feedback with demonstrations as a weakness. The earlier gradient-conflict discussion is removed, and dynamics-robustness discussion acknowledges advantages of demonstrations. The concluding simulated-feedback limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with the Optuna sampler, startup trials, search ranges, allocation rules and caps, trial counts, validation objectives, and corruption parameters. It adds training-time comparisons and a repository link for code and trained models, replacing v1's supplementary-code statement. Hardware information remains essentially unchanged; actual repository availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Optuna citation, Akiba et al. (2019), and explicitly positions MAVRL against non-amortized MCMC and post-hoc averaging through new comparisons. The related-work discussion and relationship to AVRIL remain substantially unchanged. Publication and bibliography updates for existing works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Prose revisions concentrate on method properties and experimental interpretation, alongside shortened preliminary explanations, corrected terminology, and reorganized appendices. A generic Impact Statement and front-matter edits are added. The main section sequence and most introductory, related-work, and concluding prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, removes the original method-overview diagram, merges return and EPIC tables, and replaces bold/underlined ranking marks with shaded cells. It adds comparison and ablation tables and removes the six budget-sweep tables. Transfer plots are redrawn, including a four-panel main figure; existing qualitative maps are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through direct non-variational comparisons, equal-budget controls, and corruption tests that expose limits of combining feedback. Expanded implementation details also help. These benefits are tempered by lost budget-sweep evidence and conflicting robustness-protocol descriptions: Appendix C attributes downstream tests to equal-budget checkpoints, while Section 6.3 describes fixed-allocation budgets. The added controls and qualifications support a modest net improvement, with reproducibility concerns limiting the gain.
